answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using time-locked collateral bonds. Before a node can whisper tasks across the network, it must lock funds in an escrow contract subject to slashing. This stake provides the structural timber for peer discovery, anchoring ephemeral agents to records as durable as marble. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of locked liquidity per identity. However, deposit thresholds disadvantage resource-poor agents and concentrate power among wealthy operators.
